_note: Fictional hackathon entry. Everything true about the project is here; the write-up may claim nothing else.
problem: Streets next to small creeks flood within minutes after heavy rain, and residents get no street-level warning
users: Residents of streets next to small creeks and storm drains
what_it_does: A water-level sensor on a storm drain texts nearby residents when the water rises past a threshold
existing_alternatives: Regional flood warnings from the weather service cover whole districts and arrive by app; none warns a single street from its own drain
built_during_hackathon: threshold rule that needs 2 readings in a row
pre_existing: ultrasonic sensor firmware from the team's earlier open-source university project
ESP32 board and sensor, bought before the event

ai_tools.used_for: most of the map dashboard's frontend code

limitations: no city permit to mount sensors on public drains
